perspective:
Keith’s available perspective:

- Keith knows himself as Keith Ndiaye, an African American man, a construction worker with a bachelor’s degree.
- He knows Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist/colleague at the same construction company. Their relationship is friendly but professional, mainly through Keith’s office visits for paperwork and project updates.
- Over the past few days, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him. He wondered if he had upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknowing mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and that she was sorry if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic. He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. He heard her accept and thank him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses. Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- Keith suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help. He heard her say she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- After that suggestion, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He apologized in case he had overstepped and assured her he was there to support her. He heard her say he did not overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available to chat or take a break together. He heard her thank him, say it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- He intended to maintain this supportive relationship.
